title: Dinosaur Train Morning
theme: Dinosaur train: First stop, Next stop

cards.label: Brush teeth
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: a toothbrush with toothpaste
cards.altText: A toothbrush with a line of toothpaste on it

cards.label: Swing outside
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: a playground swing
cards.altText: A playground swing hanging from a frame

plan.placement: Mount the board on the bathroom wall at her eye height, next to the sink, with both cards showing before she picks up the toothbrush.
plan.boardAction: When she finishes brushing, slide the Brush teeth card off the board, then point to the Swing outside card.
plan.reinforcement: As soon as the Brush teeth card is off, go outside with her and start the swing.
plan.ifChallengingBehavior: Stay calm, keep both cards in view, and repeat the plan: brush teeth first, then swing.
plan.generalization: Once this is easy, add one more small step before swinging, such as putting on shoes, so the board reads first, then, then.

promptHierarchy.instruction: Point at the Brush teeth card on the board.
Tap the sink or hold up the toothbrush toward her.
Brush your own teeth beside her at the sink.
Briefly guide her hand to the toothbrush, then let go.

citations: TRIAD Visual Supports and Autism (triad-visual-supports-p1-3.docx), First-Then Board and visual schedule guidance
reasoning: Brushing teeth is one non-preferred task with a clear reward straight after, so a two-card First-Then board is the smallest support that fits. Swinging outside is the Then because she already likes it and an adult can deliver it within a minute of brushing finishing.
